paper_title: Universal Activation Verbalizer: A Unified Framework for Cross-Model Activation Explanation
authors: Haiyan Zhao, Zirui He, Guanchu Wang, Ali Payani, Yingcong Li, Mengnan Du (NJIT, UNCC, Cisco Research, CUHK-SZ)
uav_method_summary: UAV trains a shared decoder (Qwen3-0.6B–32B) with a per-donor lightweight adapter that converts donor activations into n continuous soft tokens in the decoder's embedding space. Two adapter designs: MLP (LayerNorm + linear projection to bottleneck) and Q-Former (learnable query tokens + cross-attention over context slots). Decoder-side LoRA (r=64) is frozen for new donors; only the adapter (~162M–540M params) is retrained. Evaluated on last-token activations at middle-to-late layers. Metrics: ROUGE-L, BERTScore, chrF++, Token-F1. Does NOT report FVE or cosine-to-teacher.

code_search_result.paper_code_availability_statement: None — paper is a preprint (arXiv v1, 2026-05-25) with no code/weights release

blocker: UAV has no public code or model checkpoints as of 2026-06-17. The paper (arXiv preprint v1, 2026-05-25) contains no GitHub link, no HuggingFace link, and no reproducibility statement. Author's GitHub profile (hy-zhao23) contains no UAV repository. No UAV-related models found on HuggingFace Hub. Even if code were available, a metric-level head-to-head is not directly possible because UAV reports generation quality metrics (ROUGE-L, BERTScore, chrF++, Token-F1) while our method reports FVE (fraction of variance explained in activation space) and cosine-to-teacher-z — the evaluation protocols are incommensurable without substantial re-implementation of one side.

metric_incommensurability.note: UAV evaluates verbalization quality via lexical/semantic overlap with ground-truth answers on classification, fact-retrieval, and gist-summarization benchmarks (1500 examples, 15 sources). We evaluate via reconstruction fidelity in activation space (FVE) and semantic alignment with teacher verbalization (cosine). Computing FVE for UAV would require re-running their adapter inference on our 300m passage pool and capturing AR-equivalent outputs — impossible without their weights. Running our method on their benchmark would require re-extracting activations from their exact donor models and layers and computing generation-quality scores — feasible but a different experiment from what the reviewer requested.

adapter_architecture.ours: Linear enc_M (d_M -> d_shared=2048), lstsq-initialized, jointly fine-tuned during AV SFT; followed by linear dec_M (d_shared -> d_M), refit post-hoc via direct lstsq on AR predictions
adapter_architecture.uav: MLP or Q-Former adapter converting activations to n=8-128 continuous soft tokens in decoder embedding space; ~162M-540M parameters per donor

decoder.ours: Qwen3-1.7B + LoRA r=32, trained for verbalization on 10k passages; injection via marker token ㈎ at embedding layer
decoder.uav: Qwen3-0.6B to Qwen2.5-72B decoder with LoRA r=64 (132M params) decoder-side; soft token prepended to prompt

activation_position.ours: Mean-pool fp32 over content tokens at depth-fraction 0.5 layer
activation_position.uav: Last-token activations at middle-to-late layers (evaluated layer-wise)

universality_mechanism.ours: Single shared AV/AR trunk; new model gets linear enc/dec adapter fit closed-form via lstsq (~seconds, zero GPU); model identity injected as plain text tag in prompt
universality_mechanism.uav: Shared frozen decoder-LoRA; new donor requires training a new adapter (~162M-540M params) via gradient descent on labeled QA data

training_regime.ours: SFT then optional GRPO RL on AV; AR trained separately as reconstruction head; enc_M jointly trained with AV
training_regime.uav: Two-stage: Stage 1 adapter pre-training (469k samples), Stage 2 QA fine-tuning (950k pairs)

transfer_cost_for_new_model.ours: Zero-shot via lstsq refit: closed-form, ~seconds, no labeled data needed for new architecture
transfer_cost_for_new_model.uav: Requires labeled QA data + gradient training of new adapter (162M-540M params) per new donor

recommended_paper_text: The closest concurrent work to ours is Zhao et al. (2026, arXiv:2605.25903), who propose the Universal Activation Verbalizer (UAV): a shared decoder (Qwen3 family) paired with a per-donor adapter that projects activations to continuous soft tokens. UAV is methodologically complementary but architecturally different in three key ways: (i) UAV uses a trained MLP or Q-Former adapter (162–540M parameters) per donor model, requiring labeled QA data and gradient training for each new architecture, whereas our approach fits a linear adapter (enc_M) closed-form via lstsq in seconds with no labeled data; (ii) UAV operates on last-token activations, while we mean-pool in fp32 (a choice we show prevents silent fp16 overflow on attention-sink channels); (iii) UAV evaluates via generation quality metrics (ROUGE-L, BERTScore, chrF++) against ground-truth QA answers, whereas we evaluate reconstruction fidelity in activation space (FVE) and semantic alignment with teacher verbalization (cosine-to-teacher-z). These evaluation protocols are incommensurable, and UAV has not released code or checkpoints (arXiv preprint v1, 2026-05-25), precluding a numeric head-to-head on shared activations. The key practical differentiator is zero-shot extensibility: adding a new architecture to our pool requires no GPU and no labeled data (lstsq on raw activations), whereas UAV requires a full adapter training run per donor.
